source_of_the_question.summary: Three different acceptance rules feed one findings page; the published-model rule includes between-subject variability only, so it is lenient where the model is imprecise and too sharp where it is not (Kim in Bridoux moderate: 0.25% inside the limit).

approved_by_owner: 12 November 2026: scope the four lenalidomide published-model checks; margin 5%.
question: For Hughes 2019 and Kim 2026 against kidney-function groups, which verdicts hold when the uncertainty of the published estimates is added, and which sit too close to a limit to call?

scope.endpoint: Each check's own primary endpoint: the exposure ratio of the mild, moderate and severe groups to the normal group (AUC to infinity for the first three; dose-normalised AUC24 for Bridoux), in every scenario of the check's plan.
scope.not_in_scope: The pathway-model checks (95% interval of the observed mean) and the time-course checks (90% interval of the observed geometric mean) answer a different question; they keep their rules and get a one-line label naming the rule. Other drugs follow in a later plan version once their bootstrap intervals are extracted and reviewed.

rule.simulation: Each check's own simulation code, scenarios, group sizes, covariate construction and between-subject variability, unchanged, called through optional hooks that leave the checks' own results unchanged (their reproduction tests pass).

parameter_uncertainty.method: intelligence_store/parameter_draws.py: each published estimate drawn from a two-piece log-normal with median at the estimate and 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles at its published bootstrap 95% interval, independently (covariance not published).

hughes_2019.note: KTR does not enter AUC or the ratio, so it is not drawn.

kim_2026.estimates: every parameter with a bootstrap interval and not fixed (unbound CL/F, V1, Q, V2, fraction unbound, the eGFR coefficient, the two BSA coefficients)

rule.total_note: 200 x 50 = 10,000 virtual trials per scenario, the same number each check used.
rule.seed_note: Scenario i of a check uses seed + 1000 i; one parameter set of each model is drawn per outer step, then that step's virtual trials.

classes.consistent: observed ratio inside the 5th-95th percentile of the simulated ratios, and not within the margin of either limit
classes.model_under_predicts: observed above the 95th percentile, beyond the margin
classes.model_over_predicts: observed below the 5th percentile, beyond the margin
classes.indeterminate: observed within 5% (relative) of either limit, or the class differs between any of the five seeds

reported: every (check, scenario, model, group): observed ratio, simulated 5th/50th/95th percentile, class under each seed, verdict v2, verdict v1, margin to the nearest limit
the list of every verdict that changed from v1
on the findings page: one line per check naming the rule that judged it (all checks, not only these four)
old_verdicts: Not changed. The v1 reports stay as committed; v2 verdicts are reported beside them.
blindness: Not blind. Every observed value used here was seen before this plan; the dataset ledger records the uses as checked_not_blind.

executable.dry_run: tests/test_acceptance_rule_v2.py runs the rule end to end on synthetic observed ratios with few draws; nothing is run on the observed ratios before this plan is committed.

not_this: Not a new check of any model and not a blind test.
Parameter uncertainty is a lower bound: the papers publish no covariance and no bootstrap distributions.
A consistent verdict is not validation; an inconsistent one does not say why.
